newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India buys 210,000 tns of kerosene in Oct tender.
newsitem.headline: India buys 210,000 tns of kerosene in Oct tender.

text.p: State-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) has bought five cargoes of superior kerosene totalling 210,000 tonnes in its tender for October delivery, traders said on Monday.

But IOC did not award a second purchase tender for 45,000 tonnes of kerosene to be delivered during October 1-5 to Madras or Haldia on the Indian east coast, traders said. The second could have been cancelled, they added.

They said in the first tender India bought four cargoes of 45,000 tonnes each for delivery to the east coast on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f), while one cargo was bought on a free-on board (fob) basis.
State-owned Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC) was awarded four cargoes, three of which were at a premium of $2.30 per barrel to MidEast spot quotes, c-and-f east coast.
KPC also sold the 30,000-tonne fob cargo, which would be delivered to the Indian west coast, at a 65-cent premium to MidEast quotes.
US major Mobil was awarded the remaining cargo to the east coast at around $2.25 per barrel over MidEast quotes, c-and-f basis.
Traders said the awarded prices were aggressive considering the strong market in the Mideast where jet-kerosene fuel premiums were hovering at 90 cents to $1.00 per barrel.
IOC had cancelled its previous two tenders to import kerosene for August and September deliveries.
